title: Beautiful Move Alert
reviewNotes: Montage, captions and native complete later diagrams reviewed. Begin immediately before e8=Q at121 seconds in the complete eight-piece later diagram: White Kh1/e7 against Kd3/Bb4/c6/d5/g6/h5. Native25 confirms e7 and all four black pawns; native26 confirms promotion. The earlier knight interference, a-pawn sacrifice and both bishop-capture branches remain source context outside this proof. Promotion leaves eight pieces, not seven. A complete finite White strategy checks all eighteen Black replies through captures into exact supported White-winning endings, preserving every uncaptured pawn. The three guided continuations after the source promotion are independent representative replies, not a recovered source game score.
transcript: It was a long and hard game. And now white finds himself in this position where it seems like despite having the extra pawn, black has the bishop against the knight. And he's going to have an easier time trying to deal with these white pawns. And the black king is very active. As a matter of fact, he's going to pick up this pawn on the next move. But white is not a fool and he doesn't resign. He decides to push the H pawn, sacrificing it to the black pawn. Of course, if black doesn't take, we're simply promoting. And now he follows up with another sacrifice with G6. And again, the pawn has to be taken because otherwise it's going to promote. And now, white has successfully created a passed pawn. But there is one problem. If white now pushes this pawn, black is going to be able to stop it with bishop to A3. And there is no progress to be made. So, is this the end? Should white now resign? Well, not exactly. There is one incredible move that not only saves the game but wins for white and that is the beautiful and stunning [music] knight to B4 sacrificing the knight two different ways. But the idea is that we are blocking the view of the bishop. So if the king takes we can now simply [music] push and there is no way to now stop this pawn after any move. White is going to get a queen and easily win this game. And some of you might think, well, Peter, this doesn't make any sense. The bishop can simply take the knight, and now it's still stopping the pawn. But you see, white has seen an incredible idea. A4. And now there are two pawns that are threatening to simply run to promotion. And conveniently, [music] this bishop is preventing the king from running to stop the pawn. So this bishop is now overloaded, having to deal with two pawns at the same time. And after any move by black, white is now going to sacrifice this pawn. The bishop has to stop it. But now E7 is preparing to promote to a queen. And white is going to [music] win this game.
